w: In the evening Pramukh Swami Maharaj was going for darshan at the Smruti Mandir. A devotee was standing near the mandir gate with a second-hand tractor. He wanted it sanctified. Swamishri fulfilled his wish and asked, "How much did it cost?" "1,80,000 rupees."
"How much? 1,80,000... so much for a second-hand one?!" Swamishri was surprised.
On the way, Swamishri asked Aruni Bhagat, who does seva in agriculture at Sarangpur, "How much does a new one cost?"

Hearing the price, Swamishri was alarmed. The devotee's money had been lost! Under the dome he began making enquiries about this with Jodhani Saheb. He asked Yogmuni Swami, "Won't the seller take it back? The price for a second-hand one is very high. Moreover it has been used for 14 years."
"He will take it! He is known to us." Swamishri began his circumambulation. On the way back to his residence, he signalled to Yogmuni Swami to bring that devotee along.

After his meal Swamishri met him again. He explained to him, "My good man! This is a loss! The tractor has been used for 14 years. On top of that you have to pay 1.5% interest. You do not have enough money arranged. How will you manage it all? Do this: let us persuade him and return the tractor. It would be better to buy a new one than this." The man did not agree. He said, "Bapa! All that is fine. Now please bless us that we pay off the remaining money soon." Swamishri became sad.
Swamishri asked, "All right, if you do not wish it, never mind. But tell me, how much land do you have?"

Then Swamishri asked for full information about his farming. Finally he said, "Looking at your farming, it seems you will find it hard to pay the instalments. So hire out the tractor to others too. You will earn money from that. Otherwise this will not be affordable." Swamishri tried everything to make him happy. But what can the guru's knowledge do for one who has no understanding?

In the afternoon a major officer from the Border Security Force, Shri Thakursing came for Swamishri’s blessings. He then asked Swamishri, "I wish to tread the path of spirituality. Can you guide me with your words of wisdom?"

Swamishri, "Meditate on God and chant His holy name. And then by reading holy scriptures and the spiritual association with a holy sadhu will bless you with knowledge." Shri Thakursing, "Is it possible to attain moksha in this birth?’
Swamishri, "Yes, it is possible. When you find a holy sadhu then he will free you of your baser instincts and worldly desires. Through him you will get liberation..."

In the evening assembly Swamishri said, "Once one has attained or realised the knowledge of atma and Paramatma there is no need for any other knowledge. We too have to realise this knowledge so that the soul can experience eternal happiness. Gunatitanand Swami says remember God and you will experience happiness. So one should engage in the business of bhajan.

"When one suffers a big loss in business one gets tensed and anxious. Then one lapses into drinking, meat eating and gambling. But to relieve oneself from misery one must remember God and pray to Him..."
After Swamishri's morning puja, a special assembly in honor of Harikrishna Maharaj was held.

Blessing the assembly, Swamishri said, "Whatever one does should be to please God. Do not have any other wish. If one desires other things, one will get only that much. But, even then, those things do not come with us (after death) and perish. But if one does as per the wish of God, He gives everything. He gives worldly happiness and divine bliss. He gives peace in one's worldly duties and gives the bliss of atma and the abode of Paramatma." At the end of the assembly, Swamishri was garlanded with an 84 inch garland of 548,400 sesame seeds, and an 84 inch garland of 6,484 elaichis and 3,484 lavings devotionally made by the women devotees of Badalpur.

In the evening, Swamishri departed from Surendranagar towards Sarangpur. On arriving at the outskirts of Acharda, the local Darbars were waiting by the roadside. Swamishri stopped to bless them. Further, on arriving at Chachana village, the entire village folks had gathered for Swamishri’s darshan. Swamishri halted and accepted their garlands. Proceeding ahead Swamishri sang the arti and ashtaks in the car. The next stop was at Rangpur village. Swamishri performed the pujan and arti rituals of the murtis at the newly inaugurated BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir. After sanctifying the mandir with holy flower petals Swamishri attended the satsang assembly arranged on the village outskirts. After accepting the formal honours, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Through the grace of God, your devotion and love a mandir has been built. The mandir belongs to all because God belongs to all. There are no distinctions of caste or colour. Those who worship Him, He belongs to them. The sun, rain, trees and rivers are for all people. They do not segregate anyone.”

At 8.00 pm Swamishri departed from Rangpur and arrived, after a tiring schedule, in Sarangpur at 8.35 pm. He was welcomed by the tunes played by BAPS Swaminarayan Vidyamandir Band. After having Thakorji’s darshan Swamishri briefly blessed the satsangi devotees.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj began his walk at 7:25. When Swamishri sat on a chair in between to rest, Dr Nikul measured his blood pressure as he did every day. His blood pressure was a little high just then. Swamishri showed curiosity, so Dr Nikul and Yogicharan Swami explained the reasons why blood pressure rises.
Dr Nikul said, "If there is stress, tension or anger, blood pressure rises."
Yogicharan Swami said, "All that happens to people like us, it does not happen to Swamishri!"

Swamishri said, "God has created this world. 'Jene rachyu aa jagat... bhatbhatnu re...' (He who created this world of so many kinds...). We may wonder why he did it like this. The thought may come, how will this happen and what will happen? But whatever happened, happened! We turn the mala. That is what we know how to do. There is katha (spiritual discourse), so there is no problem. By God's grace, we should stay happy doing katha and bhajan. If we are troubled, others will be troubled too, won't they!" In this natural way, Swamishri spoke of the state of knowledge.

st.t: Earth Hour Celebration at Swaminarayan Akshardham
w: On 23 March 2013 from 8:30 pm to 9:30 pm, Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi joined the international community in participating in the Earth Hour celebration. For one hour, Swaminarayan Akshardham supported its continual commitment for environmental conservation by switching off its lights. In the fourth year of its participation in Earth Hour, Swaminarayan Akshardham continues to support environmental projects that promote the awareness and education of a cleaner and safer planet. Around the world, Earth Hour is embraced by the global community, transcending race, culture, age and economics as individuals take leadership in their communities in the pursuit of a cleaner and safer planet. The purpose of celebrating ‘The Earth Hour’ is to save electrical power, and to take a stand against climate change. The purpose was to stop the degradation of the earth’s natural environment and build a future where people live in harmony by reducing light pollution and the carbon footprint. Earth Hour has now a global sustainability movement in which all seven continents participate, along with world famous and iconic places like Sydney Opera House; the Harbour Bridge, the Empire State building, Swaminarayan Akshardham Mandir, India Gate, Gateway of India and other historic places under the Archaeological Survey of India in Delhi.

After his meal, before going to his room, Mahant Swami Maharaj passes by very calmly, showering his gracious glance on every devotee. Today a small child, Sharad Chavda, was standing nearby. Seeing him, Swamishri said, "He raises his hand in every section." When the volunteers of each section raise their folded hands, Swamishri puts even his meal second and casts his compassionate glance on every single volunteer.
This means that Swamishri meets every devotee who raises a hand not just with his eyes, but with his mind too.

Mahant Swami Maharaj reached the abhishek mandap by golf cart. As soon as he got down from the golf cart, he took the hands of two small children standing there, Aarav Dave and Nilkanth Parekh, and began to walk. Revealing the secret, Swamishri said, "These children had made a wish." Everyone was curious. The sadhus immediately asked the two children, "Had you made such a wish?"
Both children said "Yes."
Today, in the meeting hall outside Mahant Swami Maharaj's room, a ten year old boy, Tilak Dave, had settled down on a seat. He wished to recite before Swamishri a passage he had learnt by heart.
The sadhus told him, "Swamishri has now gone to rest. It will be difficult to get this chance today."

But this boy had had an intense wish since the morning. No chance had come, yet without losing faith he chose to sit outside Swamishri's room and wait. Suddenly at 9.30 the door of Swamishri's room opened, and to everyone's great surprise, it was Swamishri himself. Swamishri expressed a wish to go and bathe. The sadhu present ran to call the attendant sadhu. On seeing Swamishri, Tilak was beside himself with joy. He told Swamishri his wish. Swamishri sat down right next to him on the sofa. Tilak eagerly began his recitation. Swamishri listened to it with great interest and attention.

When the recitation was over, Swamishri gave him warm blessings, sent for a chocolate and fed it to him as prasad (sanctified food) with his own hand. Not only that, out of joy he also embraced him of his own accord.
It is said, "For one who has faith, spiritual endeavour is completed sooner." Today Swamishri, the friend of children, showed everyone this in person.

Mahant Swami Maharaj was now leaving to bless the satsang of South Africa. On seeing Harshadbhai Rana standing there to see him off, Swamishri recalled, "At the time of Yogibapa's last trip, you wore a polka dot muffler and looked like a dashing young man."
Everyone was dazzled by Swamishri's sharp memory. The person himself may have forgotten who wore what and when, but Swamishri remembers!!

Today Mahant Swami Maharaj came by helicopter to Jomo Kenyatta International Airport to travel from Nairobi to South Africa. There was still time before the plane took off. Two devotees asked Swamishri, "Pramukh Swami Maharaj told us to live in this country like guests. But in your blessings here you said that there is going to be great prosperity here. So what should we do? Should we expand our business here? Just give us your blessings that we progress a great deal."
Swamishri said, "In this world, everything goes on. We should look to Akshardham."

But the devotees wanted blessings for this world only. So they said, "Through your company, Akshardham is already ours. And you yourself, before us, are Akshardham in person. But please also bless us that we progress in business."
Swamishri said, "Take whatever comes to you naturally. Do not rush about too much. Do not do it at the cost of satsang."

The Gunatit Satpurush once again firmly taught us, "Do not strive for the place from which you will suddenly have to pack up and leave, but strive for that place from which you will never have to leave, even in millions of ages." But the waywardness of the soul is such that somehow it just does not understand this.
On the flight from Nairobi to Lenasia

Mahant Swami Maharaj finished his meal and rinsed his mouth. Then he remained sitting at the place for wiping hands, as if waiting for something. When the attendant noticed, he quickly picked up the napkin spread on Swamishri's lap and went to give it to him, but Swamishri said "No." For a moment the attendant was unsure: "What does Swamishri want?" With a gesture, Swamishri asked for tissue paper. At once both dry and wet tissues were offered. Swamishri wiped his hands with them.

Then, revealing the secret, he said, "If we wipe our hands on this (white) napkin, it will get stains of turmeric and so on, and however much the person whose turn it is washes it, they will not come out."
The attendants exclaimed, "Oh...h...!!"

Truly! The feeling in Swamishri's heart was beyond imagining. Who would worry so much about some unknown person who washes the napkins? If he worries this much even about a stranger, how much he must worry about those who sit in his lap!

Mahant Swami Maharaj had embraced all the sadhus. With this in mind, Hariprakashdas Swami asked Swamishri, "Swami! Today you embraced us in this way, but what are the means by which you would come forward and embrace us yourself?"
"Seeing everyone as free of faults." Then he added, "Then the work is done."

st.t: Earth Hour 2024 Observed at Swaminarayan Akshardham, New Delhi
w: Swaminarayan Akshardham in New Delhi participated in Earth Hour 2024, organized by the WWF (World Wide Fund for Nature), in support of protecting our planet.

Earth Hour encourages individuals, communities and organizations to turn off their lights for one hour to symbolize a commitment to positive environment impact. BAPS Mandirs turned off its non-essential lights to observe Earth Hour from 8:30 to 9:30 pm on 23 March 2024.
Earth Hour is the the world’s largest environmental event and a global movement which unites millions of people across the globe showing commitment to the planet.
Inspired by His Holiness Mahant Swami Maharaj, BAPS is involved in Earth Hour and many other sustainability initiatives as part of a broader commitment to support positive environmental practices.
